ai_analysis.summary: This promotional post presents an end-to-end Azure Data Engineering architecture in which source systems feed ADF pipelines, ADLS Gen2 provides raw storage, Databricks performs Bronze, Silver, and Gold transformations, Synapse SQL Pool supports curated analytics, and Power BI provides reporting. It characterizes ADF as an orchestration tool and Databricks as a large-scale transformation platform. The post also describes a claimed retail scenario involving more than 20 million daily transactions, multiple ERP systems, and near-real-time dashboards, where parallel ADF activities, Spark optimization, and Delta Lake partitioning reportedly reduced pipeline runtime from three hours to 40 minutes. It does not provide implementation details for the individual optimizations or define the purposes of the Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers.

interview_questions.question: Explain the end-to-end Azure Data Engineering architecture presented in the post.
interview_questions.answer:
A strong answer traces the flow from source systems through ADF pipelines and ADLS Gen2 raw storage to Databricks transformations, Synapse SQL Pool, and Power BI.
It assigns orchestration to ADF, large-scale transformation to Databricks, curated analytics to Synapse SQL Pool, and reporting to Power BI.

interview_questions.question: How do ADF and Databricks differ, and how do they work together?
interview_questions.answer:
A strong answer identifies ADF as the orchestration platform and Databricks as the large-scale transformation platform.
It explains that the platforms work together rather than treating them as interchangeable ETL tools.

interview_questions.question: A retail pipeline takes three hours to run. Which optimization approach does the post present, and what result does it report?
interview_questions.answer:
A strong answer identifies parallel activities in ADF, Spark optimization, and Delta Lake partitioning as the listed changes.
It reports that the combined changes reduced execution time from three hours to 40 minutes for a scenario involving more than 20 million daily transactions and near-real-time dashboards.

interview_questions.question: Which components provide orchestration, raw storage, transformation, curated analytics, and reporting in the described architecture?
interview_questions.answer: A strong answer maps ADF to orchestration, ADLS Gen2 to raw storage, Databricks to Bronze, Silver, and Gold transformations, Synapse SQL Pool to curated analytics, and Power BI to reporting.
